title: cad.like.audio/host@1
description: The CAD.Like.audio host bridge: same-origin window.postMessage between the CAD editor (in an iframe, or a window it popped out to) and the softapp hosting it. Every message is an object { protocol: 'cad.like.audio/host@1', type, ...body }. $defs 'toCad.<type>' are what a host may send; 'toHost.<type>' are what the CAD sends. Fields not listed are ignored by the receiver, so a new optional field stays @1; renaming or removing one is @2 (see hostBridge.ts, CHANGING IT). Validate with ../validate.mjs; samples.json carries one sample of every message. BLOCK EDITORS reverse the roles: when the CAD opens a block-editing softapp in an iframe of its own (SoftappBlockBridgeModal), the CAD is the PARENT; 'toEditor.<type>' are what the CAD sends that editor, and the editor answers with the 'toCad.editorReady' / 'blockChanged' / 'blockSave' / 'editorClose' messages. The browser client every such softapp loads is WEB.Frontend-Assets FrontEnd/shared/apk-softapp.js (window.APKSoftapp.connectHost).
x-transport: window.postMessage, targetOrigin = window.location.origin; the receiver drops anything whose origin or source is not its peer

xy.description: A point [x, y] in drawing units: mm, always (2.11.0, cad-1 — the CAD keeps its drawing in mm and its units choice is display only).

size.description: [w, h] in metres: a fixed-size block. Absent: an area finish.

mark.description: One thing the host draws under a marks key (hostMarks.ts).

session.description: The CAD's whole drawing session (SavedSession) — what the browser autosaves, without the sign-in. version 2 (2.11.0, cad-1): every number is mm and units is only how lengths are shown; version 1: the numbers are in units (the CAD scales such a session to mm when it opens it).

toCad.hello.description: Resend view, geometry and mirror now. bimDrops (2.10.0): the host takes a part dropped from the BIM library itself — the CAD hands it over as toHost.bimDrop instead of placing its own block. library (2.13.0, ROAD-3603): the host shows the BIM library itself — the CAD's 📚 Library and 📖 Catalog ask it with toHost.library instead of opening their own sash.

toCad.fit.description: Zoom to the drawing, or to box (drawing units) when given. inset (px) is canvas the host keeps covered — the box is framed in what is left; minZoom (px per drawing unit) is the least zoom: a box that would need less is shown from its top-left corner at that zoom.

inset.description: px of the canvas the host covers (Library Equipment's sash)

toCad.mirror.description: Put the primary Virtual Mirror axis at x (enabled defaults to true).

toCad.sheet.description: Jump to the drawing on that layer, making it current; draw seed there first if the layer is empty.

toCad.palette.description: The host's materials and products. A new palette replaces the last.

toCad.arm.description: Pick a palette item for the user to place next (null disarms).

toCad.place.description: Palette products onto the sheet as the user's own blocks, one undo step.

toCad.layer.description: Make sure a layer exists (not made current), re-colour it, set its finish, its lineweight and its IFC classification.

lineweight.description: hundredths of a millimetre, snapped to a DXF step; null back to Default. Host block line work on the layer is drawn in proportion (thinner below 0.25 mm too).

entity.description: Every edge on the layer is one IfcWall in the IFC export (cad-4).

predefinedType.description: An IfcWallTypeEnum value: STANDARD, PARTITIONING, SOLIDWALL, MOVABLE, …

isExternal.description: Pset_WallCommon.IsExternal, as the host states it (2.11.0); absent: not said.

loadBearing.description: Pset_WallCommon.LoadBearing, as the host states it (2.11.0); absent: not said.

acousticRating.description: Pset_WallCommon.AcousticRating as written — STC 52, Rw 45 dB (2.11.0); never parsed. 1–255 characters once whitespace is collapsed; an empty one is not said.

fireRating.description: Pset_WallCommon.FireRating as written — EI 60, 2 HR (2.11.0); never parsed. 1–255 characters once whitespace is collapsed; an empty one is not said.

ifc.description: How the IFC export classifies the layer's linework; null takes it off (the edges are drawing again).

toCad.move.description: Set where placed products sit, off the undo stack.

toCad.remove.description: Take placed products out, one undo step.

toCad.repaint.description: Make painted regions another palette item, one undo step.

toCad.spaces.description: The drawings kept on the sheet as named windows onto it: bounds [x1, y1, x2, y2].

fit.description: 'own': this space frames itself (a Simulation group); default 'shared': every host space at the scale that fits the largest.

toCad.walls.description: Reshape the room from the host's plan (hostWalls.ts).

toCad.layers.description: Layers on or off by name.

toCad.select.description: Select here what the host picked; host [{ key, ref }] shows those of its own schematic blocks picked.

toCad.marks.description: Replace everything drawn under key with items; ignored when hash is already on the sheet.

toCad.schematic.description: The host's devices as BIM blocks with ports, not line work (hostSchematic.ts). Replaces everything placed under key: the CAD builds each block from its part (partToDefinition) and resolves each terminal to a port itself. A placement's ports are the terminals that instance showed beyond its part's. portals: { ref: { terminal: far } }, far a string (a patch-bay position, grey) or { text, wired, to? } (another block, accent; to { drawing, refdes?, port? } when it is on another drawing). A hash already on the sheet is ignored.

to.description: The far end is on another drawing (ROAD-3666): drawing names it (the capsule says ⧉ drawing); a click sends the host `drawing` { name, refdes?, port? }.

toCad.schematicMove.description: Set where some of the host's schematic placements stand, without rebuilding them (hostSchematic.ts moveHostSchematic) — a host moving its blocks with its own layout. Off the undo stack.

toCad.session.description: Ask for the whole drawing session; answered with toHost.session. With format 'ifc' the answer also carries the drawing as IFC4X3_ADD2 STEP text (src/io/ifc), the document a host saves as its .ifc.

format.description: 'ifc': answer with the session AND its IFC4X3_ADD2 twin (toHost.session ifc).

toCad.handover.description: The host is opening this editor in a window of its own at #/drawing?host=…&resume&handover=<token>: offer the drawing to that window CAD to CAD (BroadcastChannel 'cad.like.audio/handover', hostHandover.ts), so the host never carries the session. The window says toHost.ready once it has it.

token.description: 1–64 of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ - (the CAD ignores any other); it pairs one docked CAD with one window.

toCad.open.description: Put a session on the sheet, replacing what is there (one undo step): the native session, or an IFC4X3 file (ifc), which wins when both come.

ifc.description: A whole-model ISO 10303-21 STEP text (IFC4X3_ADD2), as toHost.session ifc gives it or another tool wrote it: read by importIfc, linework, walls, rooms and placed parts.

toCad.floorplan.description: Open a floor plan the user picked in the host as a new drawing.

file.description: A File (structured clone, not JSON): a .dxf, an .ifc (opened as the drawing, as toCad.open ifc), or an image to trace.

toCad.dxf.description: Ask for the sheet as Download DXF writes it; answered with toHost.dxf (hostPick.ts).

toCad.kicad.description: Ask for the sheet as File › Export KiCad writes it: a KiCad 9/10 project (the symbols by the KiCad Library Conventions, the BIM part in APK_ fields); answered with toHost.kicad (src/io/kicad/kicadSheet.ts). `connections` (the schematic shape) are wires the host keeps as its own line work — the Simulation's routes — joined into the nets; `groups` the host's own frames ({ name, refs: the refs it placed }), drawn as titled frames; `name` the project's file stem.

toCad.tool.description: Put a tool in the user's hand, as its toolbar button would (hostPick.ts); an id this editor does not have is ignored. The Simulation asks for 'select'.

toCad.editorReady.description: A block editor in the CAD's iframe is up and listening; the CAD answers with toEditor.load.

toCad.blockChanged.description: The user changed the block in the editor (not saved yet): the CAD may show it is dirty.

toCad.blockSave.description: Store this block in the CAD drawing under meta.blockName (one undo step).

toCad.editorClose.description: The editor asks the CAD to close it.

toHost.ready.description: The CAD is up and listening. A host resends its palette and spaces on every ready.

toHost.view.description: The world→screen transform and where the canvas sits in this window. units is what zoom is per: 'mm' from 2.11.0 (cad-1), whatever lengths are shown in.

toHost.geometry.description: The visible sheet as walls, closed rooms and palette patches (sceneForHost), plus the marks hash on the sheet per key. units says what the numbers are in: 'mm' from 2.11.0 (cad-1), whatever lengths are shown in.

size.description: [w, h] the block as drawn (its outline's extent, centred on at) — bigger than the host's seat when the part needs more room

toHost.mirror.description: The Virtual Mirror: whether Symmetrical Mode is on and every axis x.

toHost.selection.description: Every change of selection here (selectionForHost); host [{ key, ref }] names the host's own schematic blocks picked (a Select press on one picks it).

ifc.description: Present when toCad.session asked for format 'ifc': the drawing as IFC4X3_ADD2 STEP text, the lossless twin of session (IfcProject → Site → Building → Storey 'Level 0' → IfcSpace per room; walls IfcWall; placed BIM parts occurrences of their library type; mm).

toHost.pick.description: A click (count 1) or double-click (count 2) on the sheet, where it landed — so a host can hit-test the pins inside its own marks (hostPick.ts). A press that travelled more than a few pixels was a drag and is not sent.

tool.description: the active tool; a host acts on 'select' only

client.description: [x, y] client pixels in the CAD's window

host.description: on one of the host's own schematic blocks: { key, ref, terminal? } (terminal: the caption of the port clicked), or { key, group } inside one of its groups (hostDrag.ts)

toHost.dxf.description: The answer to toCad.dxf: the sheet as a DXF file's text.

toHost.kicad.description: The answer to toCad.kicad: the project's files by name (<name>.kicad_sch, <name>.kicad_pro, sym-lib-table, one <Library>.kicad_sym per symbol library), every one text, kept together in one folder; `zip` the same files as one .zip, base64, for a host that downloads rather than writes a folder.

toHost.bimDrop.description: A part dragged from the BIM library (application/x-apk-bim, apk.bim.library@1) and dropped on the sheet, handed to a host that said hello { bimDrops: true } instead of being placed as the CAD's own block (ROAD-3595): bim is the part, ref its BIM reference, at where it was let go (drawing units).

blockMeta.description: What travels with a block between the CAD and its editor. Every field is optional; an editor keeps what it does not understand and sends it back.

blockName.description: The CAD block (Doc.blocks key) this edit belongs to.

blockDoc.description: The block itself: the editor's own document, opaque to the transport. When the CAD stores it as a symbol it reads name, description, basePoint, lines, arcs, circles, texts and fills (drawing units, mm).

toEditor.load.description: The CAD hands the editor the block to edit (the CAD block of that name, or a fresh stub). Sent on every toCad.editorReady and when the iframe loads.

toEditor.request.description: The CAD's "Save into CAD": answer with toCad.blockSave of what is on screen now.

toHost.library.description: The user pressed 📚 Library or 📖 Catalog in a CAD whose host said hello { library: true } (ROAD-3603): the host opens, switches or closes ITS library — one library per sheet. lens is the library app's lens: 'part' (📚 Library) or 'catalog' (📖 Catalog).

toHost.drawing.description: A fly capsule whose far end is on another drawing (a portal with to.drawing) was clicked (ROAD-3666): a host with pages opens that drawing — the Simulation switches to the page so named — and may frame refdes there. port is the far port when the capsule named one.
